draft.title: Using metalanguage
card: Metalanguage is the set of terms used to talk about how a text is made. Using the exact term shows which choice the writer made.
Motif
an image, word or idea that returns through a text, such as a broken clock that appears in many scenes.
Juxtaposition
two things placed side by side so that their difference stands out, such as a luxury party followed by a scene in a cold shelter.
Characterisation
the ways a writer builds a character, through what they say, do and think, and how others see them.
draft.remember: Name the exact term, then explain what it does for the reader and the ideas.

a.q: A novel mentions a locked gate in chapters 1, 5 and 9, each time when a character feels trapped. Which term names this technique?
opts: Motif
Juxtaposition
Characterisation
Narrative voice
a.why: The gate is an image that returns through the text and links to the same idea each time, so it is a motif. Juxtaposition needs two contrasting things placed side by side, which is not what repeats here.
a.clue: Think about something that keeps coming back.

b.q: Which sentence from a student paragraph uses metalanguage well?
opts: Juxtaposing Ana's empty home with a loud market shows her loneliness
The writer uses a good technique to make Ana seem very lonely
The writer shows Ana's loneliness by describing her home and market
Ana is lonely, and this makes readers feel sorry for her
b.why: The first option names juxtaposition and explains what the contrast shows. The second and third are vague and name no term. The fourth only retells the story and names no technique.
b.clue: Look for a precise term plus its effect.
